topic: What happens if you fall into a black hole
title: What Happens If You Fall Into a Black Hole?
hook: If you fell into a black hole, you'd die in the strangest way possible.

scenes.narration: If you fell into a black hole, you'd die in the strangest way possible.
scenes.image_prompt: supermassive black hole with glowing accretion disk

scenes.narration: Falling feet first, gravity pulls on your feet much harder than on your head.
That difference stretches you thinner and thinner. Stephen Hawking called it spaghettification.
But here's the twist. Near a supermassive black hole, you could cross the edge in one piece.
Our galaxy's center hides one. Sagittarius A star weighs about four million Suns.
From far away, a friend would see you slow down, turn red, and fade, never quite falling in.
So the scariest part isn't the fall. It's that the universe would never see you land.

claims.claim: Tidal forces stretch an infalling object (spaghettification); Hawking popularised the term in A Brief History of Time
At a supermassive black hole you can cross the event horizon before being torn apart (NASA Goddard simulation, J. Schnittman 2024)
Sagittarius A* has a mass of about 4.3 million solar masses
A distant observer sees an infalling object redden, dim and never cross the horizon
